title: The IELTS exam explained — every section, every question type
meta_description: A complete guide to IELTS Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking: timings, question types, band descriptors, raw-score tables and the mistakes that cost the most marks.

props.heading: Know the test before you sit it.
props.intro: Most candidates lose marks to the format rather than to their English. Here is the whole exam laid out — what each section asks, how long you get, and what each band actually means to a university.
rows: Two conversations and two monologues, from an everyday enquiry through to an academic lecture. Played once only.
Spelling and number formats — a correct answer written wrongly scores zero.
Academic: three long texts of increasing difficulty. General Training: notices, adverts and workplace documents.
Timing. You need roughly 200 words a minute to finish, and True/False/Not Given is the most-failed type.
Task 1 — a report on a chart or process (Academic) or a letter (General). Task 2 — a 250-word argumentative essay, worth twice as much.
Answering a related question rather than the one asked. Task 2 has five question types and five different structures.
Part 1 familiar questions, Part 2 a two-minute long turn from a cue card, Part 3 abstract discussion with the examiner.
Running out of things to say in Part 2, and one-line answers in Part 1 that cap you at Band 5.
props.footnote: Total test time about 2 hours 45 minutes. Listening, Reading and Writing are sat in one sitting with no breaks; Speaking may be the same day or up to seven days either side.

props.heading: What your band actually means.
props.lead: Bands are reported in whole and half scores. Your overall is the average of the four skills, rounded to the nearest half — which is why a single weak skill drags everything down.

rows.title: Expert user
rows.description: Full operational command. Appropriate, accurate and fluent with complete understanding.

rows.title: Very good user
rows.description: Fully operational with only occasional unsystematic inaccuracies. Handles complex argument well.
rows.used_for: Oxford, Cambridge, competitive law and medicine.

rows.title: Good user
rows.description: Operational command with occasional inaccuracy. Handles complex language and detailed reasoning.
rows.used_for: Most Russell Group postgraduate. Nursing and medical registration. Australia and Canada PR.

rows.title: Competent, upper
rows.description: Effective command despite some inaccuracy. The single most requested score.
rows.used_for: Standard postgraduate entry across the UK, Australia and Canada.

rows.title: Competent user
rows.description: Generally effective command; can use and understand fairly complex language in familiar situations.
rows.used_for: Undergraduate entry, foundation and pathway programmes.

rows.title: Modest, upper
rows.description: Partial command. Copes with overall meaning but makes many mistakes.
rows.used_for: Foundation year, some vocational courses, pre-sessional English.

rows.title: Modest user
rows.description: Partial command, handles basic communication in own field.
rows.used_for: Pre-sessional English. Below most academic requirements.

rows.title: Limited and below
rows.description: Basic competence limited to familiar situations; frequent problems with understanding and expression.

notes: Rounding: an average of 6.25 rounds up to 6.5; 6.1 rounds down to 6.0.
Validity: results are normally accepted for two years.
Retakes: unlimited, and single-skill retakes are now available at many centres.

props.heading: Choosing the wrong one is expensive.
props.body: Listening and Speaking are identical. Reading and Writing are not — and a university will not accept a General Training result, however high the band.

cards.title: Take Academic for study
cards.body: University at any level, and professional registration in medicine, nursing, law, engineering and accountancy.

cards.title: Take General Training for migration
cards.body: Permanent residency and work visas for Australia, Canada, New Zealand and the UK, plus secondary school and vocational training.

cards.title: If you are not certain, take Academic
cards.body: It is accepted for almost everything General is, but not the reverse. We check your target institution's requirement before you book.

side.intro: The same level of English on every scale — useful when a university lists a TOEFL requirement and you have an IELTS band.
side.footnote: Approximate concordance for planning. Always confirm the exact requirement with the institution — many set a minimum per skill as well as an overall.

props.heading: Five stages. Nothing is guessed.
props.lead: Most preparation fails for one reason: students practise without ever checking what they got wrong. Bloom is built to make that impossible.

steps.title: Placement test
steps.body: Twenty-five minutes across grammar, vocabulary, reading, listening, writing and speaking. It returns a CEFR level, a band per skill, and your strongest and weakest areas — from what you actually did, not from what you told us.

steps.title: Your English profile
steps.body: An honest picture: where you sit on the CEFR scale, what your estimated band is on every exam scale, and which first-language errors we will be watching for as a speaker of your language.

steps.title: A plan built from it
steps.body: A day-by-day schedule to your test date, weighted towards your weakest skill, with a mock every Saturday and a checkpoint every fortnight. Tick each block off as you do it.

steps.title: Practice with real feedback
steps.body: Write an essay, get a band against all four descriptors and every error explained. Record a cue card, get fluency, vocabulary, grammar and pronunciation scored separately. Your recurring mistakes are collected into an error bank.

steps.title: Measured, then adjusted
steps.body: Every scored activity moves your estimate. When a mock says your reading is the problem, next week's plan changes. You always know what to revise today and what you have already mastered.

props.heading: Feedback is the whole product.
props.body: Anyone can sell you practice papers. Half a band takes roughly a hundred focused hours — and those hours only count if something tells you, precisely, what went wrong.

cards.title: Every essay marked against the four official criteria
cards.body: Task Response, Coherence and Cohesion, Lexical Resource, Grammatical Range and Accuracy — separately, with a band each.

cards.title: Sentence-level corrections, not a grade
cards.body: The wrong version, the right version, and why. Repeat offenders go into your personal error bank.

cards.title: Errors targeted to your first language
cards.body: Articles for Hindi and Urdu speakers, plural and tense endings for Mandarin speakers, final consonants for Vietnamese speakers.

cards.title: Spaced repetition that decides for you
cards.body: 570 academic words scheduled so the ones you miss come back tomorrow and the ones you know disappear for a month.

side.wrong: People is becoming more dependent on technology.
side.right: People are becoming increasingly dependent on technology.
side.why: “People” is an irregular plural and always takes a plural verb. “Increasingly” is also more precise than “more” here.
